Present: Mr. Adarsh Jain, Advocate for the petitioners
 Mr. Ankur Mittal, Addl. A.G., Haryana with
 Mr. Saurabh Mago, Dag, Haryana.
 ****
 Sureshwar Thakur, J. (Oral)
1.

The prayer made in the instant petition is for the quashing of the notification issued under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act of 1894') (Annexure P-2), and, to the declaration, as became issued under Section 6 of the Act of 1894 (Annexure P-3).
2.

The challenge, as made to the annexures (supra), is rested on the premise, that since the petitioners become entitled to a lapsing declaration, thus in terms of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 (for short 'the Act of 2013'), therefore, the launching of the acquisition proceedings through the annexures (supra) be made lapsed.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Evidently the notifications (supra) were issued respectively in the year 1982, and, in the year 1985, and, they culminated in an award becoming rendered in the year 1985.

sentences.text: 4. The purpose of acquisition is for developing Sectors 11-12 and 25 Part-II, Panipat.
However, for the reasons to be assigned hereinafter, this Court finds no merit in the instant petition.

5. The principal reason for declining the reliefs (supra), as claimed by the writ petitioners, becomes planked on the factum, that the acquiring authority concerned, has adduced cogent discharging evidence, in satisfaction of the duo of parameters, as encapsulated in a verdict rendered by the Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Indore Development Authority versus Manohar Lal and others, reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129, inasmuch as, para 3.3 of the reply on affidavit,
furnished to the instant petition by the respondents concerned, does unfold thereins, (i) that the said parameters do become satisfied thus, through rapat possession No. 79 of 4.11.1985, thus possession of the acquired lands becoming assumed, by the acquiring authority concerned, (ii) that in terms of Section 31 of the Act of 1894, the assessed compensation amount becoming deposited,
before the authority concerned, but on pronouncement of award in the year 1985, for thereby its becoming released viz-a-viz the land losers concerned.
6.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority versus Manohar Lal and others, reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the above adduced discharging evidence is in evident satisfaction of the duo of parameters (supra), as spelt in Indore Development Authority's case (supra), besides when both events (supra)
evidently occurred prior to the coming into force of the Act of 2013.
Therefore, thereby the reliefs (supra), as claimed in the instant petition, thus cannot become assigned to the land losers concerned.

Moreover, when apparently, the acquired lands are required for subserving a public purpose, thereby also this Court does not deem it fit, and, appropriate to scuttle the public purpose,
through assigning reliefs (supra) in favour of the land losers concerned.
authenticity of this order/judgement CWP No. 30041 of 2018 -3- 2023:PHHC:159472-DB 7.
In aftermath, this Court finds no merit in the instant petition, and, the same is hereby dismissed.
8. The pending application(s), if any, is/are also disposed of.
(SURESHWAR THAKUR) JUDGE (SUDEEPTI SHARMA) JUDGE December 13, 2023 Gurpreet

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
5. The principal reason for declining the reliefs (supra), as claimed by the writ petitioners, becomes planked on the factum, that the acquiring authority concerned, has adduced cogent discharging evidence, in satisfaction of the duo of parameters, as encapsulated in a verdict rendered by the Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Indore Development Authority versus Manohar Lal and others, reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129, inasmuch as, para 3.3 of the reply on affidavit,

before the authority concerned, but on pronouncement of award in the year 1985, for thereby its becoming released viz-a-viz the land losers concerned.
6.
Since the above adduced discharging evidence is in evident satisfaction of the duo of parameters (supra), as spelt in Indore Development Authority's case (supra), besides when both events (supra)
evidently occurred prior to the coming into force of the Act of 2013.
Therefore, thereby the reliefs (supra), as claimed in the instant petition, thus cannot become assigned to the land losers concerned.

Moreover, when apparently, the acquired lands are required for subserving a public purpose, thereby also this Court does not deem it fit, and, appropriate to scuttle the public purpose,
through assigning reliefs (supra) in favour of the land losers concerned.
In aftermath, this Court finds no merit in the instant petition, and, the same is hereby dismissed.
